quotes.quote: Each InnoDB table has a special index called the clustered index that stores row data.
each record in a secondary index contains the primary key columns for the row, as well as the columns specified for the secondary index.
With the exception of spatial indexes, InnoDB indexes are B-tree data structures.
The default size of an index page is 16KB.
If index records are inserted in a sequential order (ascending or descending), the resulting index pages are about 15/16 full.
A 6-byte DB_TRX_ID field indicates the transaction identifier for the last transaction that inserted or updated the row.
A 7-byte DB_ROLL_PTR field called the roll pointer.
a row is not physically removed from the database immediately when you delete it with an SQL statement.
InnoDB only physically removes the corresponding row and its index records when it discards the update undo log record written for the deletion.
This removal operation is called a purge
A consistent read means that InnoDB uses multi-versioning to present to a query a snapshot of the database at a point in time.
A record lock is a lock on an index record.
A gap lock is a lock on a gap between index records
A next-key lock is a combination of a record lock on the index record and a gap lock on the gap before the index record.
InnoDB uses next-key locks for searches and index scans, which prevents phantom rows
The redo log is a disk-based data structure used during crash recovery to correct data written by incomplete transactions.
recovery starts at the latest checkpoint LSN.
InnoDB automatically rolls back uncommitted transactions that were present at the time of the crash.
An undo log is a collection of undo log records associated with a single read-write transaction.
3/8 of the buffer pool is devoted to the old sublist.
The doublewrite buffer is a storage area where InnoDB writes pages flushed from the buffer pool before writing the pages to their proper positions in the InnoDB data files.
can perform a multiple-statement transaction by starting it with an explicit START TRANSACTION or BEGIN statement and ending it with a COMMIT or ROLLBACK statement.
When deadlock detection is enabled (the default) and a deadlock does occur, InnoDB detects the condition and rolls back one of the transactions (the victim).
The default isolation level for InnoDB is REPEATABLE READ
Consistent reads within the same transaction read the snapshot established by the first read.
If a table has no PRIMARY KEY or suitable UNIQUE index, InnoDB generates a hidden clustered index named GEN_CLUST_INDEX on a synthetic column that contains row ID values.
A 6-byte DB_ROW_ID field contains a row ID that increases monotonically as new rows are inserted.
A COMMIT means that the changes made in the current transaction are made permanent and become visible to other sessions.
A ROLLBACK statement, on the other hand, cancels all modifications made by the current transaction.
By default, MySQL starts the session for each new connection with autocommit enabled, so MySQL does a commit after each SQL statement if that statement did not return an error.
If autocommit mode is enabled, each SQL statement forms a single transaction on its own.
Isolation is the I in the acronym ACID
InnoDB offers all four transaction isolation levels described by the SQL:1992 standard: READ UNCOMMITTED , READ COMMITTED , REPEATABLE READ , and SERIALIZABLE .
a non-locking SELECT statement presents the state of the database from a read view which consists of transactions committed before the read view was created
The buffer pool is an area in main memory where InnoDB caches table and index data as it is accessed.
the buffer pool is divided into pages that can potentially hold multiple rows.
data that is rarely used is aged out of the cache using a variation of the least recently used (LRU) algorithm.
The header is used to link together consecutive records, and for row-level locking.
The passage of data through redo log files is represented by an ever-increasing LSN value.
dirty pages are flushed from the buffer pool to tablespace data files
InnoDB can find a good copy of the page from the doublewrite buffer during crash recovery.
rolls back one of the transactions (the victim)
In MySQL 9.7, InnoDB is the default MySQL storage engine.

quotes.what: ACID with commit rollback crash recovery
quotes.quote: Its DML operations follow the ACID model, with transactions featuring commit, rollback, and crash-recovery capabilities to protect user data.
Row-level locking and Oracle-style consistent reads increase multi-user concurrency and performance.
The ACID model is a set of database design principles that emphasize aspects of reliability that are important for business data and mission-critical applications.
so that data is not corrupted and results are not distorted by exceptional conditions such as software crashes and hardware malfunctions.
The atomicity aspect of the ACID model mainly involves InnoDB transactions
The consistency aspect of the ACID model mainly involves internal InnoDB processing to protect data from crashes.
an UPDATE or DELETE of a row does not immediately remove the old version of the row.
